# A pane whose home node collapsed comes home in an arbitrary zone

## Context

Measured on a downstream dock consumer while verifying the pop-out round trip end to end (2026-09-03). The tear-out and the return both work; the pane just does not come back where it left.

```
BEFORE pop-out : ["Dokumente", "Editor", "Verbindung"]     Verbindung is the RIGHT EDGE zone
AFTER pop-out  : ["Dokumente", "Editor"]                   aux-tabs emptied and was removed
AFTER close    : ["Dokumente", "Verbindung", "Editor"]     back in the CENTRE, beside Dokumente
```

Same component instance returns (`neo-webstudio-connection-info-1` both times, and Neo does not reuse ids), so object permanence holds. Only the placement is wrong.

## The Problem

`Workspace#reintegrateTearOutItem` resolves the pane's home like this:

```js
placement  = me.tearOutPlacements[itemId],
storedHome = placement && doc?.nodes?.[placement.tabsNodeId]?.type === 'tabs' ? placement.tabsNodeId : null,
fallback   = storedHome || Object.entries(doc?.nodes || {}).find(([, node]) => node.type === 'tabs')?.[0],
```

`tearOutPlacements[itemId]` records the exact pre-detach placement — `captureTearOutPane`'s sibling discipline, and the right intent. But the `storedHome` guard requires that node to **still exist**, and for a single-pane zone it never does: detaching the last item empties the node, an empty tabs node is removed, and an emptied edge zone collapses. So `storedHome` is `null` and the fallback is *the first tabs node in document order* — an arbitrary zone that merely happens to be enumerated first.

The failure is therefore guaranteed, not occasional, for exactly the panes most likely to be torn out: a pane that is alone in its zone. A pane sharing a node with siblings returns correctly, because its node survives the detach.

Two consequences worth separating:

- **The user's layout silently changes.** A right-edge inspector comes back as a centre tab. Nothing reports it, and a saved perspective committed afterwards persists the wrong arrangement.
- **The recorded intent is discarded.** `tearOutPlacements` holds a `tabsNodeId` that is no longer resolvable, and nothing tries to reconstruct what it describes.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` — `reintegrateTearOutItem(itemId, pane)`: the `storedHome` / `fallback` resolution above, then `applyDockZoneOperation({operation: 'addTab', itemId, tabsNodeId: fallback})`.
- `tearOutPlacements[itemId]` is written pre-detach and deleted at the top of `reintegrateTearOutItem`, so the record's only consumer is the branch that cannot use it once the node is gone.
- Node removal on empty is correct behaviour and is not in question here (docking design record §2.7): the defect is that reintegration has no way to reverse it.
- `Document` owns the node vocabulary, so reconstructing a zone is a reducer concern rather than something the return path should hand-roll.

## The Fix

Make the recorded placement sufficient to rebuild its own home, rather than only to find one that survived.

`tearOutPlacements[itemId]` should capture enough of the pre-detach position to reconstruct it — the owning zone and the node's position within its parent, not just a `tabsNodeId` string. On return, when the stored node is absent, reintegration recreates it in that position and adds the item there; when it is present, today's behaviour is unchanged.

The arbitrary `Object.entries(...).find(...)` fallback should remain only as the genuine last resort — a document with no recorded placement at all — and it is worth making that path say so rather than looking like a considered choice.

The sibling anchor is what makes the record outlive its own parent: a two-child split collapses into the sibling, so `parentId` is unresolvable in exactly the case the record exists for | no parent slot → `null` | JSDoc | capture/restore round-trip arms |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — §2.7's collapse-on-empty stays exactly as it is; this restores the inverse for a returning pane and changes no zone semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 A pane that was **alone** in an edge zone returns to that edge zone after its vessel closes, asserted by the committed document's node topology rather than by tab order.
- [ ] AC-2 Red-first: the same witness fails at the current head, reporting the pane in the first-enumerated tabs node.
- [ ] AC-3 A pane that shared its node with siblings still returns to that node — the surviving-home path is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-4 A pane alone in a **centre split** child returns to that position in the split, not merely to some tabs node.
- [ ] AC-5 Object permanence is unregressed: the returning pane is the same component instance, asserted by component id, not by DOM node identity — a DOM node cannot survive a move between documents, so identity must be read off the instance.
- [ ] AC-6 With no recorded placement at all, the last-resort fallback still returns the pane somewhere valid rather than dropping it.
- [ ] AC-7 Exact-head unit + component suites green.
- [ ] AC-8 A recorded home whose slot is now **occupied by a different node** does not overwrite that occupant: an edge zone re-docked while the pane was out keeps its new occupant, and the returning pane resolves elsewhere or through the last resort. Red-first — a single-slot write with no ownership check silently orphans the occupant, which loses a pane other than the one being restored.

## Out of Scope

- Collapse-on-empty itself; removing an emptied node stays correct.
- The vessel lifecycle, adoption, and the declining-hook family — #18151 and its subs.
- Restoring geometry (split sizes) beyond the node's position; a returning pane may inherit the current sizes.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reading tab order as placement.** The symptom surfaced as a changed tab sequence, but the assertion has to be on the document's nodes: a correct tab order over a wrong zone would pass, and the two are only coincidentally related.
- **Suppressing collapse-on-empty to keep the home alive.** That would leave empty zones behind for every tear-out and contradict §2.7 — the return path is what needs to reverse it, not the detach.
- **Treating this as rare.** It is guaranteed for a pane alone in its zone, which is the common tear-out case; the passing case is the one with siblings.
- **Guarding only existence, never ownership.** A recorded coordinate can be *invalid* or *taken*, and restoration code naturally checks the first and forgets the second. An additive slot (a split's `children`) is immune; a single-value slot (an edge zone's `nodeId`) is not. My own AC set missed this until review — corrected as AC-8.
- **Asserting DOM identity for AC-5.** A node moved between documents is necessarily re-created. I measured this and briefly read it as a lost instance; the component id is the only honest witness.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-03T07:24:47Z

Fix in [#18165](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/18165), all 7 ACs green.

**One place your Fix section needed extending, worth recording here rather than only in the PR:** `{owning zone + index within parent}` is sufficient for an edge zone, and not for AC-4. Removing a child from a two-child split leaves one child, and `normalizeTree` collapses that split too — so the recorded `parentId` is unresolvable in precisely the case the record exists for.

The record therefore also carries a **sibling anchor**: the node that split collapsed *into*, which is by definition still present. Restore is a ladder — recorded parent still holds the slot → re-split against the sibling, restoring orientation, side and ratio → fail closed.

Your `Out of Scope` line on geometry was right in a way I initially coded past: `normalizeTree` resets a split's sizes to equal when a child collapses, so the pre-detach ratios are gone *before* restore runs. Preserved instead are the returner's recorded share and the survivors' ratios to each other; the code now states that constraint rather than implying a guarantee it cannot make.

Red-first control (AC-2) against the merge base: model arms 8 failed / 1 passed, workspace arms 2 failed / 3 passed — the three passing at baseline are the AC-3/AC-6 unchanged-path controls.

Review finding from @neo-opus-vega. An edge zone holds ONE node per key and setZoneNodeId

the slot while the pane was out. The displaced node stays in document.nodes referenced by

The sequence is ordinary, not exotic. A vessel window is long-lived, so "pane alone in the right
edge is torn out, user docks something else to that edge, vessel closes" is a normal session.

It also inverts this seam's own stated priority. Losing the position is bad and losing the pane
is worse - and the path traded a stranger's pane for the returner's position.

The distinction the code was missing: a recorded coordinate can become INVALID (the node is gone,
which the sibling anchor exists for) or OCCUPIED (someone else took the slot). Restoration guards
existence by instinct and forgets ownership. The single-slot edge-zone path now asks both; the
split path was already safe, but only because splicing is additive rather than by intent, so the
JSDoc says so.

An occupied slot resolves to nothing and falls through to the existing "no longer resolves"
error, which reintegrateTearOutItem already handles by retrying through lastResort(). No new
policy: the returner lands somewhere valid and the occupant keeps its zone.

Guard admits the node its OWN slot - a check that only asked "is anything there?" would send a
pane away from a home it never lost. Both cases have arms.

Three arms: model-level occupancy (the occupant stays reachable from the root, the document is
returned untouched), model-level re-entry, and a workspace-level round trip that docks a node
into the recorded edge while the vessel is open and asserts the occupant keeps both slot and
item. Removing the guard turns the first and third red on their own assertions.

Vega also flagged Contract Ledger drift on #18164 - the ticket predicted a narrower surface than
shipped, including Operations.operations growing from 15 to 16, which consumers read. She is
